issue.title: orchagent busy-wait loop in cSONiC containers when PortInitDone is never set

failure.body:
## Description

On the SONiC Virtual Switch (VS) platform, `orchagent` occasionally enters a tight CPU spin loop in its CRM (Counter Resource Monitoring) thread, consuming 100% of a CPU core indefinitely. The issue is observed in `docker-sonic-vs` containers used as cSONiC neighbors in sonic-mgmt testbeds, but likely affects any VS deployment.

## Symptoms

- `orchagent` process pegged at ~100% CPU
- `rsyslogd` also elevated (~55% CPU) due to log flooding from orchagent
- Container overall CPU usage ~158% (orchagent + rsyslogd combined)
- Occurs on some containers but not all, even in the same testbed (suggests a timing/race condition at startup)

## Root Cause Analysis

The CRM thread in orchagent continuously polls SAI resource availability via `object_type_get_availability()`. On the VS SAI implementation, many of these queries return `SAI_STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED`. The CRM thread appears to retry without any backoff or rate-limiting, resulting in a tight poll loop.

Evidence from `sairedis.rec` on an affected container shows continuous rapid-fire queries:

```
2026-02-28.<IPV6>.277910|q|object_type_get_availability|SAI_OBJECT_TYPE_SWITCH:oid:0x21000000000000|SAI_ROUTE_ENTRY_ATTR_IP_ADDR_FAMILY=SAI_IP_ADDR_FAMILY_IPV4
2026-02-28.<IPV6>.278251|Q|object_type_get_availability|SAI_STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED|COUNT=0
2026-02-28.<IPV6>.278499|q|object_type_get_availability|SAI_OBJECT_TYPE_SWITCH:oid:0x21000000000000|SAI_ROUTE_ENTRY_ATTR_IP_ADDR_FAMILY=SAI_IP_ADDR_FAMILY_IPV6
2026-02-28.<IPV6>.278704|Q|object_type_get_availability|SAI_STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED|COUNT=0
... (repeating continuously)
```

## Reproduction

1. Deploy a sonic-mgmt KVM testbed with cSONiC neighbors (`-k csonic`)
2. After `add-topo` completes, check CPU usage: `docker stats --no-stream`
3. Some cSONiC containers will show ~158% CPU; inside, `orchagent` is at 100%

In our test, VM0100 and VM0101 were healthy (0.2% CPU), while VM0102 and VM0103 were affected (158% CPU). The only difference is startup timing.

## CPU Evidence

```
VM0100 orchagent:  0.0% CPU,  <IPV6> cumulative
VM0101 orchagent:  0.0% CPU,  <IPV6> cumulative
VM0102 orchagent: 99.9% CPU,  <IPV6> cumulative (in ~45 min uptime)
VM0103 orchagent: 99.9% CPU,  <IPV6> cumulative (in ~45 min uptime)
```

## Environment

- Platform: VS (docker-sonic-vs)
- Usage: cSONiC neighbors in sonic-mgmt KVM testbed
- Host OS: Ubuntu with KVM/Docker

## Suggested Fix

The CRM polling loop should:
1. Skip or cache results for resource types that return `SAI_STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED`
2. Add a backoff/sleep between polling cycles to prevent tight loops
3. Optionally, disable CRM polling entirely on VS platform where resource counters are not meaningful

## Impact

- Wastes ~2-3 CPU cores per testbed (when multiple neighbors are affected)
- Floods syslog, making it harder to debug real issues
- Functional impact is low — BGP and data plane still work correctly

## Related

- sonic-net/sonic-swss#189 (different orchagent CPU issue — unresolved next hops)

resolution.title: Fix orchagent 100% CPU spin when gOrchUnhealthy is set
resolution.description:
## Description

Fix orchagent consuming 100% CPU when `gOrchUnhealthy` is permanently set after a SAI API failure. Two root causes addressed:

1. **Syslog spam**: The error log was called every select loop iteration (~80K/sec), causing rsyslogd to also consume ~55% CPU. Fixed by moving the log into the existing `SELECT_TIMEOUT` periodic block (once per second).

2. **epoll_wait spin**: When `gOrchUnhealthy` is set, internal `Selectable` objects remain in a "ready" state, causing `epoll_wait()` to return immediately with timeout=0 instead of blocking for `SELECT_TIMEOUT` (1000ms). This causes the select loop to spin at ~160K iterations/sec. Fixed by adding an explicit `sleep_for(SELECT_TIMEOUT)` when both `gOrchUnhealthy` is set and select returns `TIMEOUT`.

### Root Cause
PR #4040 introduced `gOrchUnhealthy` flag that gets set permanently when SAI hostif creation fails during startup. On SONiC VS (docker-sonic-vs) used as cSONiC neighbors in testbeds, a race condition between orchagent and syncd causes this failure reliably on some containers.

### Impact Before Fix
- orchagent: **100% CPU** (epoll_wait spin at 160K calls/sec)
- rsyslogd: **~55% CPU** (processing ~37K syslog messages/sec)
- System effectively unusable for its intended purpose

### Impact After Fix
- orchagent: **0% CPU** (select loop blocks properly for 1 second intervals)
- rsyslogd: **0% CPU** (1 log message per second)

### Validation
- Tested on SONiC KVM testbed with 4 cSONiC neighbors (docker-sonic-vs)
- Before fix: VM0102/VM0103 at 100% CPU
- After fix: All 4 neighbors at 0% CPU
- Confirmed via `strace`: `epoll_wait` now blocks with 1000ms timeout
- All 4 BGP sessions Established and stable

### Changes
- `orchagent/orchdaemon.cpp`: Add `sleep_for(SELECT_TIMEOUT)` when `gOrchUnhealthy && ret == TIMEOUT`
- `orchagent/orchdaemon.cpp`: Move `gOrchUnhealthy` error log into `SELECT_TIMEOUT` periodic block
- `orchagent/orchdaemon.cpp`: Add `#include <thread>` for `std::this_thread::sleep_for`
- `tests/mock_tests/test_failure_handling.cpp`: Unit test for `gOrchUnhealthy` flag behavior

Fixes: #4273
